title: HIP LDPC belief-propagation prototype
description:
Implement and evaluate a HIP/ROCm batch LDPC normalized min-sum belief-propagation prototype.

## Background

LDPC BP dominates decoding time in coded simulation campaigns. The prototype batches frames on GPU while preserving CPU/GPU correctness and comparing against the best current production CPU path.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] GPU Tanner graph representation matches CPU sparse matrix structure, including check/variable offsets and mate indices.
- [hard] HIP kernels implement check-node NMS, variable-node update, and syndrome or early-termination support.
- [hard] Safe Rust wrappers and `gf2-coding` integration are feature-gated behind `hip`; default workspace builds succeed without ROCm.
- [hard] CPU/GPU correctness fixtures cover Hamming, 5G NR BG2, and DVB-T2 short Rate1/2 with specified LLR tolerances and exact hard-decision equality where required.
- [hard] GPU LDPC BP is at least 3x faster than the best existing production CPU path at the selected design workload.

## Notes

Spec doc: `dev/plans/hip_gpu_prototype_wave.md`. Existing design doc: `dev/active/gpu-batch-ldpc-bp-plan.md`. This story depends on GPU evidence infrastructure.
